title: Volkswagen workers protest against austerity measures in Emden

tea.why: Volkswagen workers protested against massive austerity plans, potential plant closures, and job cuts.
tea.want: Protesters demanded the protection of their collective agreements, rejecting wage freezes and cuts to benefits.
tea.changed: Nov 24: First round of wage negotiations began following protests in Emden and concluded without an immediate agreement.

summary: Volkswagen workers and labour representatives held a noisy protest outside the Nordseehalle in Emden, Germany, coinciding with the start of crucial wage negotiations. Organised by the IG Metall union, participants rallied against extensive austerity measures proposed by the automaker, including job cuts, plant closure threats, and rollbacks to long-standing benefits and the 35-hour workweek. Demonstrators marched with drums, sirens, and symbolic coffins to reject management's cost-cutting proposals. Following the demonstration, union and company negotiators met for their initial round of talks, which concluded without a breakthrough.
demands: Reject proposed wage freezes for 2027 and 2028
Protect the 35-hour workweek without flexible extensions
Stop cuts to bonuses and supplementary payments
Secure jobs and prevent plant closures
response: According to the sources, Volkswagen management defended the restructuring plans due to falling sales in China, high domestic production costs, and weak operating margins, entering negotiations on austerity measures while warning of potential strikes.

crowd.text: IG-Metall-Angaben versammelten sich rund 4.500 Menschen, die Polizei sprach von etwa 2.300 Teilnehmern.

updates.text: Workers gathered outside the negotiation venue in Emden with drums, sirens, and placards opposing company austerity plans.
Wage negotiations between Volkswagen management and IG Metall representatives began and ended without reaching a consensus.
